root_idea.summary: The root encompasses three principal orientations: ease or softness, ruin and loss, and persistent application.
root_idea.development: The lexical field connects easy or soft ground and the ebbing of the sea with a separate branch of perdition, loss, and destruction, while ثابر and related forms express sustained perseverance.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Quran-attested passive participle مَثْبُور.
Displayed as the Quran-attested verbal noun ثُبُور.

senses.definition: Ruined, destroyed, or brought to perdition; made to perish.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic passive-participle use describing a person in a state of destruction or ruin.

senses.definition: Deprived of good, overcome, or rendered unsuccessful; consequently lost or astray.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, the participle is also interpreted as driven away or outcast, punished or accursed, and as prevented from attaining what is good. An exegetical interpretation explains it as deficient in intellect, understood as a form of profound ruin.

senses.definition: Perdition, ruin, or destruction, including loss, corruption, and being lost, especially destruction from which there is no return.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as an accusative verbal noun in Quranic calls for destruction or perdition. It can function as singular or plural and can express a cry of woe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To confine, restrict, restrain, withhold, hinder, or prevent someone; to turn him away or back from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive; the construction may restrict someone to a thing or restrain him from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deny or debar someone from attaining what he desires; to disappoint or frustrate his desire or hope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use describing frustrated attainment or unsuccessful effort.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive away, expel, or banish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive use describing removal from a place or group.
A transitive use expressing imprecation or the laying of a curse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To destroy someone with an irreversible destruction, so that he does not rise again.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive use; distinct from the intransitive meaning ‘to perish.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perish, suffer loss, err, go astray, or become lost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive use describing a person or thing that comes to ruin or is lost.
Used with the sea as subject; the ebb exposes ground characterized as soft or easy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep to, attend to, or apply oneself constantly, perseveringly, or assiduously to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly construed with عَلَيْهِ, ‘to it’; describes sustained application to an affair or activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leap or spring upon one another in war or combat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal use describing combatants attacking one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be heavy or sluggish and hold oneself back from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنْهُ, ‘from it,’ for reluctance or sluggish withdrawal from an undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Suffering loss, erring, going astray, becoming lost, or perishing; a loser.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active-participial adjective describing one undergoing loss or ruin.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Transitive restraint, restriction, and turning away.
Intransitive perishing, loss, error, and being lost.
Persistent application to an activity or affair.
Active participle for one suffering loss or ruin.
Quran-attested ruin, deprivation, defeat, expulsion, and related interpretations.

cautions: مَثْبُور in the Quranic address admits several closely related interpretations—destroyed, deprived of good, overcome, outcast or accursed, and deficient in intellect—rather than a set of unrelated lexical items.
